title: Getscreen.me Review (2026)
intro: Getscreen.me is evaluated here as an adjacent remote access / screen-share tool — Getscreen.me is remote access and screen-sharing software for support and remote work. Free covers 1 user and ≤2 devices. Business plans combine per-user and per-device fees: Standard $5/user + $0.10/device, Advanced $8/user + $0.15/device, Enterprise $10/user + $0.20/device. Personal Lifetime one-time option. 14-day business trial. Adjacent productivity — not a project tracker. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s project-management methodology (ease of use, work planning, automation, collaboration, integrations, reporting, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Getscreen.me when remote access / screen share is the productivity job — adjacent to, not instead of, a work OS.
verdict: Choose Getscreen.me when remote access / screen share is the productivity job — adjacent to, not instead of, a work OS. Compare monday/Hive for work management, Foxit for PDF, WebCatalog for desktop app workspaces. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

faq.question: Is Getscreen.me a project management / work OS tool?
faq.answer: No. Getscreen.me is adjacent remote access / screen-share tooling. Pair it with a work OS if you also need boards, Gantt and workload planning.

faq.question: How is Getscreen.me priced?
faq.answer: Free: 1 user, ≤2 devices. Standard $5/user + $0.10/device; Advanced $8+$0.15; Enterprise $10+$0.20. Personal Lifetime one-time. 14-day business trial. Confirm live.

faq.question: Does Getscreen.me have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: Yes — a free plan is published. A free trial is documented (about 14 days). Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test Getscreen.me?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
